code.originalText: Primary care follow-up six weeks into immunosuppressive therapy, after laser capsulotomy of the right eye

text.paragraph: Six-week review on immunosuppressive therapy, one week after laser capsulotomy. [S]

Madame Curie returns six weeks after starting immunosuppressive therapy. She has had no fever, infection, or bleeding, and the bruising has lessened. She has a little more energy in the afternoons. She takes cyclosporine, eltrombopag, and acyclovir as prescribed. Ophthalmology confirmed posterior capsule opacification in the right eye two weeks ago and performed a YAG laser capsulotomy one week ago. She now reads standard print without glare, with no eye pain, redness, new floaters, flashes, or shadow in her vision. She is frustrated at being away from her laboratory. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1934-06-29; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: No ulcers, thrush, or gum swelling
Fading bruises on the shins; no petechiae
Right red reflex now clear; both eyes white and quiet

Severe aplastic anemia: pancytopenia with a low reticulocyte count, confirmed by a hypocellular bone marrow; attributed to cumulative occupational ionizing radiation; linked to the documented 1842 diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the 1934 report remains D and the radiation cause is R.
Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over decades of radium research and X-ray work
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented exposure history.
Posterior capsule opacification, right eye, after earlier bilateral cataract surgery; glare and blurred reading vision
S — Synthetic eye finding linked to the documented cataracts and operations.
Chronic radiodermatitis of the fingertips, with thin, scarred skin
S — Synthetic skin finding linked to the documented finger burns.

value.displayName: Aplastic anemia due to other external agents

list.item:
Severe aplastic anemia, early response to immunosuppressive therapy (D61.2). Early rise in counts without transfusion since the first visit: neutrophils 0.8 (from 0.4), platelets 34 (from 18), reticulocytes 31 thousand per microliter, hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL. No infection or bleeding. Creatinine 1.02 mg/dL is about 30 percent above the pre-treatment 0.78 (eGFR 61) and potassium is 4.9 on cyclosporine; ALT 31. [S]
Continue cyclosporine at the current dose until hematology reviews it, with eltrombopag and acyclovir.
Hematology contacted today to review the cyclosporine dose against a trough level, given the creatinine rise.
Repeat creatinine and potassium within a week with the weekly counts.
Formal response assessment at three months.

Posterior capsule opacification, right eye, treated (H26.491). Reading without glare one week after YAG laser capsulotomy; reading goal met. [S]
Call the same day for new floaters, flashes, a shadow, pain, or loss of vision.
Comprehensive eye examination every one to two years.
